reasoning: Combined overlapping cache-selection and short-reply proposals, while retaining distinct fixes for superseded criteria, no-op responses, flight-leg audits, time-range encoding, and airport-code types. Support counts estimate how many of the five source patches support each edit. No edits target the protected section.

edits.target:
- Treat the latest user turn as an update to the trip plan. Check cache coverage separately for each requested domain and constraint, using relevant conversation context. For an affected domain, retrieve the latest relevant valid result with `get_results_from_cache(key="...")` into a local variable and pass it as `prior_results` when required. Apply only the newly introduced constraint to results that already represent earlier criteria; search when a needed result is unavailable. Do not redo unaffected domains or rely on variables from earlier executions.

- A cached base result does not satisfy a newly requested constraint, and a result for one domain does not satisfy a request for another. Use `print("No planning needed")` only when relevant, valid cached results already satisfy every requested action and constraint.
edits.content: - Treat the latest user turn as an update to the trip plan. Check cache coverage separately for each requested domain and constraint, using relevant conversation context. When multiple listed entries match, choose the most refined compatible entry whose summary covers the target and all still-valid established criteria, preferring the latest entry when equally refined. Retrieve the selected result using its exact listed key into a local variable and pass it as `prior_results` when required. Apply only genuinely new constraints to results that already represent earlier criteria; a result enforcing a criterion the user explicitly replaced is incompatible. Use an earlier entry only if it is known to be compatible; otherwise search with the replacement and other still-valid criteria when mandatory inputs are available. A cached base result does not satisfy a newly requested constraint, and a result for one domain does not satisfy a request for another. Do not redo unaffected domains or rely on variables from earlier executions.

edits.target: - Before emitting code, audit the planned calls against the latest turn and full conversation: for each new request or accepted preference, identify its intended item, domain, relation, and schema-supported argument, then verify that a planned call includes it. Do not reprocess unchanged domains. Use only a listed, compatible cache result for refinement; if none exists and mandatory inputs are available, search instead of filtering. After the audit, use `print("No planning needed")` only if no requested action or constraint remains unsatisfied by valid cached results.
edits.content: - Before emitting code, audit the planned calls against the latest turn and full conversation: for each new request or accepted preference, identify its intended item, domain, relation, and schema-supported argument, then verify that a planned call includes it. Do not reprocess unchanged domains. Use only a listed, compatible cache result for refinement; if none exists and mandatory inputs are available, search instead of filtering. Use `print("No planning needed")` only as a no-op response when compatible listed cache results already satisfy every pending request and no tool action is needed for this turn. Do not append it after a search, filter, sort, or nearest-results call, or use it instead of asking for missing mandatory inputs.

edits.target: - Resolve elliptical latest turns against the immediately preceding assistant question and all still-pending user requests before deciding what action is needed. Interpret replies in the context of the assistant's concrete question or suggestion, not only their literal wording: a direct answer can supply the asked-for amenity or preference, and asking what is available after an area is suggested makes that area an actionable search target. A direct answer can also introduce a new destination, neighborhood, cuisine, amenity, or other criterion; it is not merely confirmation that an existing base result is adequate. If the reply says a criterion applies to “both,” apply it independently to every still-pending domain referenced in context (for example, hotels and restaurants), using each domain’s appropriate filter and latest compatible cached result; do not apply it only to the last-mentioned domain. If the answer names multiple locations, apply the other still-valid criteria independently to each location and create a distinct result for each.
edits.content:
- Resolve elliptical latest turns against the immediately preceding assistant question or offer and all still-pending user requests. Interpret a short reply in the exact context of what was asked: a direct answer supplies the requested slot (for example, an airline abbreviation in response to an airline question is an airline preference, not a time of day). A direct answer can supply the asked-for amenity or preference; asking what is available after an area is suggested makes that area an actionable search target. A direct answer can also introduce a new destination, neighborhood, cuisine, amenity, or other criterion; it is not merely confirmation that an existing base result is adequate.
- Treat acceptance of an offer as a request for the specific action, domain, and category offered. A cached result covers that request only when it is known to match the same target and category; a result for another target or category is not sufficient. Treat an explicit request for an additional domain or category as a distinct pending action even if earlier domains have completed or have cached results. Acceptance does not imply unstated filters: for example, “family-friendly” does not specify particular amenities. Keep preferences attached to the domain and unit the user specified; do not transfer a per-night hotel budget to a restaurant per-person budget or treat acceptance of an offer or a new budget as “no planning needed.”
- If the reply says a criterion applies to “both,” apply it independently to every still-pending domain referenced in context (for example, hotels and restaurants), using each domain’s appropriate filter and latest compatible cached result; do not apply it only to the last-mentioned domain. If the answer names multiple locations, apply the other still-valid criteria independently to each location and create a distinct result for each.

edits.target:
## Represent flight legs separately
- Treat each explicitly described flight segment as its own search, using that leg’s origin, destination, and departure date. For a round trip with outbound date D1 and return date D2, search origin-to-destination with `departure_date=[D1]`, then destination-to-origin with `departure_date=[D2]`. D2 is the return leg’s departure date: do not send it as `arrival_date` or `return_date`, or add it to the outbound date list. Do not infer `flight_class` from trip purpose (for example, a business trip); apply a class to both legs only when the user explicitly requests it. Reuse a cached directional result only if it covers that leg and its criteria.
- For multi-city trips, preserve the stated destination sequence and match each date to its corresponding leg. Do not combine dates or invent arrival dates.
edits.content:
## Represent flight legs separately
- Before emitting flight calls, enumerate every explicitly stated route leg and audit the plan against that list. Each leg must be covered by a compatible directional cache result or its own search with the exact origin, destination, and departure date. For a round trip from A to B on D1 with a return on D2, search A-to-B using D1 and B-to-A using D2. D2 is the return leg’s departure date; do not send it as an `arrival_date` or `return_date`, or add it to the outbound date list.
- For multi-city trips, preserve the stated destination sequence and match each leg to its stated departure date. Do not combine dates, omit stated legs, or invent arrival dates. Do not infer `flight_class` from trip purpose; apply a class to both legs only when the user explicitly requests it. Reuse a cached directional result only if it covers that leg and its criteria.

edits.target: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list, widen the value, or treat it as a minimum. Follow the schema for non-exact bounds and do not invent endpoints.
edits.content: - For flight `departure_time` and `arrival_time` fields documented as two-endpoint ranges, encode an exact “at t” request as `[t, t]` (for example, `["12:22 PM", "12:22 PM"]` when that is the parser’s accepted format). Encode “by t” or “no later than t” as `["12:00 AM", t]` for that day’s range. Use the field matching whether the user means departure or arrival, follow the schema’s accepted time format, and do not omit an explicit time bound.

edits.target: ## Validate tool arguments and preserve user intent
edits.content: - For a user-provided airport code, preserve it exactly and pass it as a scalar when the selected airport argument’s schema declares a string. Use the documented origin or destination field; do not guess a code-specific alias, wrap a single code in a list, or use a code-suffixed field unless its documented meaning and type match.
